title: Why Do So Many Traffic Stops Go Wrong?

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂安娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用观看，并免费获得一个月的所有新闻阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: A Times investigation shows that police killed 400 unarmed drivers or passengers during traffic stops over the last five years.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一项调查显示，在过去五年中，警察在交通拦截中杀害了 400 名未携带武器的司机或乘客。

sentences.en: I spoke to my colleague, David Cook-Patrick, about why so many traffic stops go wrong and why the problem is so hard to fix.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事大卫·库克-帕特里克，探讨为什么那么多交通拦截会演变成悲剧，以及为什么这个问题如此难以解决。

sentences.en: It's Monday, November 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月1日，星期一。

sentences.en: David, where did you start this investigation?
sentences.zh: 大卫，这项调查是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: Well, it started right after the conviction of Derek Chauvin, the police officer who'd pulled
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是从德里克·肖万被定罪后不久开始的，也就是那个把

sentences.en: George Floyd out of the driver's seat of a car and then killed him on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 乔治·弗洛伊德从汽车驾驶座上拉出来，然后在大街上杀害的警察。

sentences.en: There had been a number of other instances of unarmed drivers, mostly African-Americans, killed by police at vehicle stops, including Dante Wright in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 之前还发生过起其他未武装司机被警察在车辆拦截中杀害的事件，其中大部分是非裔美国人，包括明尼苏达州的丹特·赖特。

sentences.en: There was an Army Lieutenant,
sentences.zh: 还有一位陆军中尉，

sentences.en: Karen Nazario, who was pulled over in Pepper Strait in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 卡伦·纳扎里奥，她在弗吉尼亚州的温莎被拦下。

sentences.en: So we wanted to know, is this happening as often as it seems?
sentences.zh: 所以我们想知道，这种情况发生的频率真的像看起来那么高吗？

sentences.en: Unarmed drivers getting killed at vehicle stops?
sentences.zh: 未武装司机在车辆拦截中被杀？

sentences.en: And if it is happening a lot, why?
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况真的很频繁，原因是什么？

sentences.en: So what did you do to answer those questions?
sentences.zh: 那你为了回答这些问题做了什么？

sentences.en: What did you do first?
sentences.zh: 你首先做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, my colleagues in investigation, Steve Eder and Kim Barker and I began with a list of 5,000 people killed by police over the last five years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我和调查部的同事史蒂夫·埃德尔、金·巴克从过去五年中被警察杀害的 5000 人名单开始着手。

sentences.en: We got that from data put together already by the
sentences.zh: 这些数据是我们从

sentences.en: Washington Post and two research organizations mapping police violence and fatal encounters.
sentences.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》以及两个绘制警察暴力和致命冲突地图的研究组织已经整理好的数据中获取的。

sentences.en: From there, we collected all the news reports and court records and, whenever possible, audio and video recordings of these killings that we could.
sentences.zh: 在此基础上，我们收集了所有能找到的新闻报道、法庭记录，以及尽可能多的这些谋杀案的音频和视频记录。

sentences.en: And we tried to isolate the people who were killed at vehicle stops, the people who were unarmed, not carrying a gun or a knife, not threatening the police with a weapon.
sentences.zh: 我们试图筛选出在车辆拦截中被杀、且未携带武器（没有带枪或刀，也没有用武器威胁警察）的人。

sentences.en: And also, we tossed out everybody who was being pursued for a violent crime.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们剔除了所有因涉嫌暴力犯罪而被追捕的人。

sentences.en: So no bank robbers, no murderers on the run.
sentences.zh: 所以没有银行劫匪，没有在逃的杀人犯。

sentences.en: We wanted to isolate just the killings at vehicle stops that seemed the most questionable, the most potentially avoidable.
sentences.zh: 我们只想筛选出那些在车辆拦截中最存疑、最有可能本可避免的命案。

sentences.en: And what we got was about 400 drivers or passengers over that five-year period who were killed at vehicle stops.
sentences.zh: 最终我们发现在那五年期间，大约有 400 名司机或乘客在车辆拦截中被杀。

sentences.en: That's about six a month or more than one a week.
sentences.zh: 这大约是每月六人，或者说每周超过一人。

sentences.en: Six a month.
sentences.zh: 一个月六人。

sentences.en: That sounds like a lot.
sentences.zh: 听起来很多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as in other killings by American police, African Americans were disproportionately overrepresented.
sentences.zh: 而且就像美国警察造成的其他命案一样，非裔美国人的比例过高。

sentences.en: In many cases, when we talked to the families of the drivers who'd been killed, they said, you know, I don't think my relative would have been pulled over if he or she wasn't
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，当我们与遇害司机的家属交谈时，他们会说，你知道的，如果我的亲人不是

sentences.en: black.
sentences.zh: 黑人，我认为他或她根本不会被拦下。

sentences.en: Now, if you look at all of the 400 unarmed drivers we identified, in many cases, they were
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你看看我们确定的所有 400 名未武装司机，在很多情况下，他们

sentences.en: drunk or under the influence of drugs, or they had drugs in the car, or for one reason or another, they tried to flee.
sentences.zh: 喝了酒或受到药物影响，或者车里有毒品，又或者由于某种原因，他们试图逃跑。

sentences.en: But that said, none of that means they deserve to be killed by the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这并不意味着他们罪不至死，不该死在路边。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what did you find out about why these traffic stops become so violent?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于为什么这些交通拦截会变得如此暴力，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the first part of the answer comes pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，答案的第一部分很快就有了。

sentences.en: We started talking to police officers or former police officers, and the first thing they'd say is, well, people get killed at traffic stops
sentences.zh: 我们开始与警察或前警察交谈，他们说的第一件事就是，呃，在交通拦截中有人被杀，

sentences.en: because we're told that traffic stops are very dangerous to us.
sentences.zh: 因为我们被告知交通拦截对我们来说非常危险。

sentences.en: And we began looking into that.
sentences.zh: 我们开始深入调查这一点。

sentences.en: We collected training manuals.
sentences.zh: 我们收集了培训手册。

sentences.en: We interviewed trainers.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了培训员。

sentences.en: And we found out as much as we could about the process of teaching cops how to do vehicle stops.
sentences.zh: 我们尽可能多地了解了教导警察如何进行车辆拦截的过程。

sentences.en: And what we learned is that they're often told that more officers are killed stopping vehicles than in any other context.
sentences.zh: 我们了解到的是，他们经常被告知，在拦截车辆时殉职的警察比在任何其他情况下都多。

sentences.en: That's the most common way for an officer to be killed.
sentences.zh: 这是警察殉职最常见的方式。

sentences.en: In the most aggressive training manuals, they say point blank, every driver could be a killer.
sentences.zh: 在那些最具攻击性的培训手册中，他们直言不讳地指出，每个司机都可能是杀手。

sentences.en: Watch out.
sentences.zh: 当心点。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it's really drummed into them from the very beginning of their life as a police officer.
sentences.zh: 所以从他们当警察的第一天起，这种观念就被深深灌输进去了。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Throughout their training, and then repeatedly through their career at roll call briefings before they go on duty, they're shown videos that show easygoing, tolerant cops getting
sentences.zh: 在他们的整个培训过程中，以及在他们职业生涯中执勤前的点名简报会上，他们会被一遍又一遍地播放这样的视频：展示那些随和、宽容的警察

sentences.en: mowed down by drivers who whip out guns out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 被突然掏出枪支的司机无情枪杀。

sentences.en: There's one especially iconic video.
sentences.zh: 有一个特别具代表性的视频。

sentences.en: Driver, step back here to me.
sentences.zh: 司机，退回到我这里来。

sentences.en: Come on back here for me.
sentences.zh: 过来，到我这儿来。

sentences.en: An officer named Kyle Dinkheller, who pulled over a pickup truck in Georgia in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫凯尔·丁赫勒的警察，在20世纪90年代于佐治亚州拦下了一辆皮卡车。

sentences.en: Keep your hands out of your pocket, sir.
sentences.zh: 把手从口袋里拿出来，先生。

sentences.en: Sir, come here.
sentences.zh: 先生，过来。

sentences.en: Sir, come here.
sentences.zh: 先生，过来。

sentences.en: The driver jumps out, and he's jumping around like a madman.
sentences.zh: 司机跳下车，像个疯子一样上蹿下跳。

sentences.en: He's dancing.
sentences.zh: 他在跳舞。

sentences.en: Come here, sir.
sentences.zh: 过来，先生。

sentences.en: Sir, get back.
sentences.zh: 先生，退后。

sentences.en: What are you calling?
sentences.zh: 你在打给谁？

sentences.en: Sir, get back.
sentences.zh: 先生，退后。

sentences.en: Now, get back.
sentences.zh: 现在，退后。

sentences.en: Get back.
sentences.zh: 退后。

sentences.en: Sir, get back now.
sentences.zh: 先生，马上退后。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Get back.
sentences.zh: 退后。

sentences.en: Fuck you.
sentences.zh: 去你的。

sentences.en: Sir, get back.
sentences.zh: 先生，退后。

sentences.en: And he's not obeying any of the police officer's orders.
sentences.zh: 他不服从警察的任何命令。

sentences.en: Sir, get back now.
sentences.zh: 先生，马上退后。

sentences.en: And after a while...
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿……

sentences.en: I am doing my life.
sentences.zh: 我在过我的人生。

sentences.en: Get back here now.
sentences.zh: 现在给我退后。

sentences.en: Put the gun down.
sentences.zh: 把枪放下。

sentences.en: The driver pulls out a semi-automatic weapon.
sentences.zh: 司机掏出一把半自动武器。

sentences.en: Drop the gun now.
sentences.zh: 马上把枪放下。

sentences.en: And he guns down the officer right there, and it's captured on the officer's own dash cam.
sentences.zh: 他当场开枪打死了警察，这一切都被警察自己的行车记录仪拍了下来。

sentences.en: So Kyle Dinkheller has really become a martyr, and seemingly every officer I talk to knows who he is.
sentences.zh: 所以凯尔·丁赫勒真的成了烈士，似乎我交谈过的每个警察都知道他是谁。

sentences.en: And his name stands for the ever-present danger to police whenever they're pulling over a vehicle.
sentences.zh: 他的名字代表了警察在拦下任何车辆时面临的无处不在的危险。

sentences.en: That sense of peril has become so ingrained that when officers are walking over to the driver's side window,
sentences.zh: 这种危机感已经根深蒂固，以至于当警察走向驾驶座侧窗时，

sentences.en: when they're pulling over a car, they'll often put four fingers on the trunk.
sentences.zh: 在拦下汽车时，他们通常会把四根手指放在后备箱上。

sentences.en: The reason they're trained to do that is to leave fingerprints.
sentences.zh: 他们接受这种培训的原因是为了留下指纹。

sentences.en: That way, if the officer is ambushed and killed by the driver,
sentences.zh: 这样一来，如果警察遭到伏击并被司机杀害，

sentences.en: detectives, when they find the car, will know who did it.
sentences.zh: 侦探在找到汽车时就会知道是谁干的。

sentences.en: It's almost like a kind of tactile reminder of just how dangerous pulling over a car is for a cop.
sentences.zh: 这几乎成了一种触觉上的提醒，提醒警察拦下一辆车有多么危险。

sentences.en: Okay, so what I'm hearing you say is that vehicle stops are really dangerous for police officers.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我听到你的意思是，车辆拦截对警察来说真的很危险。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what this is all laying out for me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是这一切向我展示的。

sentences.en: Well, what the police are told in their training isn't really the full picture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，警察在培训中被告知的情况并非全貌。

sentences.en: Over the five-year period we looked at, 20% of all those officers killed in crimes while on duty were killed by motorists they had pulled over.
sentences.zh: 在我们调查的五年期间，所有在职期间因犯罪殉职的警察中，有 20% 是被他们拦下的驾车者杀害的。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, that is a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，这确实很多。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it's misleading.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，这也是具有误导性的。

sentences.en: It's misleading because traffic stops are the most common way police interact with civilians.
sentences.zh: 这是误导性的，因为交通拦截是警察与平民互动最常见的方式。

sentences.en: They perform tens of millions of them every year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年执行数千万次这样的拦截。

sentences.en: And when you look at the sheer number of traffic stops, each vehicle stop is really not that dangerous.
sentences.zh: 当你看看交通拦截的绝对数量时，就会发现每一次车辆拦截其实并没有那么危险。

sentences.en: In fact, there have been more than one study done that shows the chance of an officer getting killed at a vehicle stop is less than one in 3.6 million.
sentences.zh: 事实上，已经有多项研究表明，警察在车辆拦截中遇害的几率小于三千六百万分之一。

sentences.en: If you isolate just the ordinary traffic stops, you know, not chasing a felon, it's less than one in 6 million.
sentences.zh: 如果你只把普通的交通拦截单列出来，你知道的，不是追捕重罪犯，那这个几率小于六百万分之一。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: That's very small.
sentences.zh: 这非常小。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that really is a relatively small chance.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这确实是一个相对较小的几率。

sentences.en: I called some statisticians who study this kind of thing, and they said someone is more likely to die going for a horse ride or taking a swim.
sentences.zh: 我咨询了一些研究这种事情的统计学家，他们说一个人因为骑马或游泳而死亡的可能性都要更大。

sentences.en: So, even though officers are taught that traffic stops are incredibly dangerous, that's not actually true.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管警察被灌输交通拦截极其危险的观念，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's misleading.
sentences.zh: 这是有误导性的。

sentences.en: And that assumption has consequences.
sentences.zh: 而这种假设是有后果的。

sentences.en: What we see is that officers are trained to think that because it's so dangerous, they need to have total control.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是，警察受到的训练让他们认为，因为情况太危险，他们必须拥有绝对的控制权。

sentences.en: Hey, stay away.
sentences.zh: 嘿，离远点。

sentences.en: You're distracting me.
sentences.zh: 你在分散我的注意力。

sentences.en: You're going to go to jail if you interfere, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你干预的话，你要进监狱的，对吧？

sentences.en: You are interfering because...
sentences.zh: 你在干预，因为……

sentences.en: And that leads them sometimes to treat mere disobedience as a mortal threat.
sentences.zh: 这有时会导致他们将纯粹的不服从视为致命威胁。

sentences.en: To retaliate against backtalk or evasion...
sentences.zh: 对回嘴或逃避进行报复……

sentences.en: Hey, man, hands!
sentences.zh: 嘿，老兄，把手放好！

sentences.en: Hands!
sentences.zh: 把手放好！

sentences.en: Hands, motherfucker!
sentences.zh: 把手放好，他妈的！

sentences.en: ...or a lack of compliance...
sentences.zh: ……或者对不配合进行反击……

sentences.en: I'm going to shoot your fucking ass, man.
sentences.zh: 我要崩了你这个混蛋，伙计。

sentences.en: I'm going to fucking blow you that off.
sentences.zh: 我他妈要把你轰成渣。

sentences.en: Sometimes with threats of deadly force...
sentences.zh: 有时甚至伴随着使用致命武力的威胁……

sentences.en: As of your license, please.
sentences.zh: 请出示您的驾照。

sentences.en: ...or even occasionally deadly force.
sentences.zh: ……甚至偶尔会真正使用致命武力。

sentences.en: Get out of the guard!
sentences.zh: 滚出警戒区！

sentences.en: Get out of the guard!
sentences.zh: 滚出警戒区！

sentences.en: And also, it has another consequence.
sentences.zh: 此外，它还有另一个后果。

sentences.en: So, on the one hand, because of this fear, you see a very understandable kind of aggression on the part of the officers.
sentences.zh: 一方面，由于这种恐惧，你会看到警察表现出一种非常可以理解的攻击性。

sentences.en: But then, after the fact,
sentences.zh: 但随后，事后来看，

sentences.en: you also find that prosecutors and courts grant extra leeway for the use of force to police who are performing traffic stops because of the perceived danger.
sentences.zh: 你也会发现，由于所感知到的危险，检察官和法院对在交通拦截中执法的警察使用武力给予了额外的宽容。

sentences.en: So, what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 那么，这具体表现为怎样？

sentences.en: Well, we should be clear.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们应该明确一点。

sentences.en: A police officer is only allowed to use deadly force if the police officer reasonably fears an imminent threat to the police officer's life or someone else's life.
sentences.zh: 警察只有在合理担心自己或他人的生命面临迫在眉睫的威胁时，才被允许使用致命武力。

sentences.en: They're not allowed to use deadly force just to punish disobedience.
sentences.zh: 他们不允许仅仅为了惩罚不服从而使用致命武力。

sentences.en: But when you take into account the reputation for danger at these vehicle stops, prosecutors, judges,
sentences.zh: 但当你考虑到这些车辆拦截危险的名声时，检察官、法官

sentences.en: and juries are often inclined to accept that the police officer really did fear for his or her life.
sentences.zh: 和陪审团往往倾向于接受警察确实在为自己的生命安全感到恐惧的说法。

sentences.en: Even when, in fact, the actual danger is very debatable.
sentences.zh: 即便实际上，真正的危险其实非常值得商榷。

sentences.en: In our list of 400 deaths of unarmed drivers,
sentences.zh: 在我们盘点的400起无武装驾驶员死亡事件中，

sentences.en: we found dozens of cases where officers shot motorists just because the motorists were reaching for something or holding an object that turned out not to be a gun.
sentences.zh: 我们发现有数十起案件，警察向驾车者开枪，仅仅是因为对方在拿什么东西，或者手里拿的物品后来被证明根本不是枪。

sentences.en: That includes, in one case, holding a bottle of antifreeze.
sentences.zh: 其中甚至有一起案件，手里拿的是一瓶防冻液。

sentences.en: In another case, a bag of sandwiches.
sentences.zh: 另一起案件中，是一袋三明治。

sentences.en: Many times, of course, just cell phones.
sentences.zh: 当然，很多时候仅仅是手机。

sentences.en: So, it's very easy for a judge or jury to accept that the driver was reaching for something and the officer credibly believed it could have been a gun.
sentences.zh: 因此，法官或陪审团很容易接受这样的说法：司机当时在拿东西，而警察有理由相信那可能是一把枪。

sentences.en: Or perhaps the driver was revving his engine and the officer credibly believed that even if the driver was probably trying to escape, he could also run down the officer.
sentences.zh: 或者也许司机当时在猛踩油门轰鸣发动机，警察有理由相信，即便司机可能只是想逃跑，他也有可能撞倒警察。

sentences.en: So, when a vehicle is involved, given this reputation for danger, it's very easy for the officer to say to a prosecutor or a judge or a jury, look, I really did fear for my life.
sentences.zh: 所以，当涉及车辆时，考虑到这种危险的名声，警察非常容易对检察官、法官或陪审团说：听着，我当时确实在为自己的生命担忧。

sentences.en: Courts often assess the use of deadly force based only on the final moment when an officer pulls the trigger.
sentences.zh: 法院往往仅根据警察扣动扳机的那最后关头来评估致命武力的使用。

sentences.en: But we looked at more than 120 videos of those killings.
sentences.zh: 但我们查看了其中120多起此类命案的视频。

sentences.en: And we found that if you roll back the video and look at the larger context, often the story is much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，如果你倒回视频并审视更宏观的背景，通常情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, David, you said that what actually happens during these traffic stops is more complicated than what the public ends up seeing.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你刚才说，这些交通拦截过程中实际发生的事情，比公众最终看到的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: What did your reporting show?
sentences.zh: 你们的报道显示了什么？

sentences.en: Well, our colleagues in The New York Times visual investigations team isolated 120 of these videos of killings at vehicle stops.
sentences.zh: 嗯，《纽约时报》视觉调查团队的同事们挑选出了120段发生在车辆拦截现场的致命枪击视频。

sentences.en: They picked out the videos where you could really see clearly what was happening at the moment of the actual shooting.
sentences.zh: 他们挑选出了那些能真正清晰看清实际开枪瞬间情况的视频。

sentences.en: And what they found was that in 45 of these 120 cases, the officer had actually put him or herself at risk.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，在这120起案件中的45起里，警察其实是将自己置于了危险境地。

sentences.en: What criminologists call officer-created jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 犯罪学家称之为“警察制造的危机”。

sentences.en: That means the police officer had stepped in front of a moving vehicle or reached into the door or the window of a vehicle.
sentences.zh: 这意味着警察挡在了一辆行驶中的车辆前方，或者将手伸进了车门或车窗里。

sentences.en: And the officer had put his own life in jeopardy and then cited that jeopardy as a reason for killing the driver.
sentences.zh: 警察自己把生命置于危险之中，然后又以这种危险为由杀害了司机。

sentences.en: What's happening here is the officer takes a moment of disobedience and turns it into a life or death encounter.
sentences.zh: 这里发生的情况是，警察将一幕不配合的行为演变成了一场生死对决。

sentences.en: It's going to be you or it's going to be me.
sentences.zh: 不是你死，就是我活。

sentences.en: The officer says, all right, you're not listening to me and trying to flee.
sentences.zh: 警察说，好吧，你不听我的话还试图逃跑。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to make that a choice between your life and my life.
sentences.zh: 那好，我要把它变成在你死和我活之间二选一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the driver isn't exactly following orders, but the officer makes it into a life or death encounter.
sentences.zh: 所以司机并非完全服从指令，但警察把它变成了一场生死对决。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So one of the videos we looked at is the killing of a driver named Colton LeBlanc.
sentences.zh: 我们调查的视频之一，就是对一名叫科尔顿·勒布朗的司机的枪杀案。

sentences.en: Colton LeBlanc is driving his pickup truck.
sentences.zh: 科尔顿·勒布朗正开着他的皮卡车。

sentences.en: He's driving erratically.
sentences.zh: 他开车有些蛇行危险驾驶。

sentences.en: A Louisiana state trooper pulls him over.
sentences.zh: 一名路易斯安那州州警将他截停。

sentences.en: LeBlanc gets out of the car.
sentences.zh: 勒布朗下了车。

sentences.en: And he has a conversation with the trooper.
sentences.zh: 他开始与州警交谈。

sentences.en: The trooper starts out fairly polite.
sentences.zh: 州警一开始还算客气。

sentences.en: Asks for his license.
sentences.zh: 索要驾照。

sentences.en: Let's go get it, please.
sentences.zh: 去拿一下吧，请。

sentences.en: LeBlanc heads back to his car to get the license.
sentences.zh: 勒布朗返回他的车去拿驾照。

sentences.en: And that's when things start to go wrong.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，事情开始出错。

sentences.en: I can't see it.
sentences.zh: 我看不到了。

sentences.en: You can see in the video, LeBlanc is putting his foot on the brake.
sentences.zh: 你可以在视频中看到，勒布朗正把脚踩在刹车上。

sentences.en: He's reaching for the ignition.
sentences.zh: 他正伸手去够点火开关。

sentences.en: A second later, LeBlanc puts the car in gear.
sentences.zh: 一秒钟后，勒布朗挂上了档。

sentences.en: LeBlanc, at this point, is only suspected of possibly being a drunk driver.
sentences.zh: 此时的勒布朗，仅仅被怀疑可能酒后驾车。

sentences.en: Tactically, trainers would tell you the right thing for the officer to do is to let him drive away.
sentences.zh: 在战术上，培训人员会告诉你，警察最正确的做法是让他把车开走。

sentences.en: You've got his license plate number.
sentences.zh: 你已经记下了他的车牌号。

sentences.en: You could follow him.
sentences.zh: 你可以跟着他。

sentences.en: Instead, this Louisiana state trooper grabs the open door.
sentences.zh: 然而，这名路易斯安那州州警却抓住了开着的车门。

sentences.en: He hangs himself over the open door with his left hand as LeBlanc is beginning to drive away.
sentences.zh: 当勒布朗开始开车离开时，他用左手挂在敞开的车门上。

sentences.en: And he shouts to LeBlanc, stop, stop, stop the car.
sentences.zh: 他对勒布朗大喊：停车，停车，把车停下。

sentences.en: But LeBlanc is not stopping the car.
sentences.zh: 但勒布朗并没有停车。

sentences.en: And at that point, the trooper has hung himself off the open door of a moving pickup truck.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，州警整个人挂在了一辆行驶中的皮卡敞开的车门上。

sentences.en: And his life really is in jeopardy.
sentences.zh: 他的生命确实陷入了危险之中。

sentences.en: He pulls out his gun with his right hand and he shoots LeBlanc three times.
sentences.zh: 他用右手拔出枪，向勒布朗连开三枪。

sentences.en: In the torso, the arm, and the ear.
sentences.zh: 击中了躯干、手臂和耳朵。

sentences.en: LeBlanc died in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 勒布朗在医院死亡。

sentences.en: So, you're saying that when you look at the shooting itself, you're only really getting half the picture.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，当你只看枪击本身时，你其实只看到了事情的一半。

sentences.en: Because when you rewind the film and you look at the whole thing, you understand that it's not always as simple as the officer was afraid for his life.
sentences.zh: 因为当你倒回录像并纵观全局时，你就会明白，事情并不总是像“警察当时害怕自己的生命受到威胁”那么简单。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Advocates for the police would say, look, this driver was disobedient and actually threatened the police officer.
sentences.zh: 警察的辩护者会说，看呐，这名司机不服从管理，实际上威胁到了警察。

sentences.en: Which is true.
sentences.zh: 这确实是真的。

sentences.en: But at the same time, choices by that officer turned what might have been an innocuous or routine encounter into a life or death challenge that ended in the driver dying.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，该名警察的选择将一场本可能是无害的或例行公事的遭遇，变成了一场以司机死亡告终的生死考验。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That this disobedience becomes a potentially lethal thing.
sentences.zh: 这种不服从行为变成了一件潜在致命的事情。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Disobedience becomes a capital crime.
sentences.zh: 不服从变成了一种死罪。

sentences.en: So, David, as you describe all of this to me, there's one thing I'm kind of getting stuck on.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，当你向我描述这一切时，有一点我一直有点想不通。

sentences.en: Which is, if police officers are trained that stops are so dangerous and often put themselves in unnecessary risk when they do them,
sentences.zh: 那就是，如果警察受到的训练是拦截检查非常危险，且他们在执行时经常让自己承担不必要的风险，

sentences.en: then why not do fewer of them?
sentences.zh: 那为什么不减少拦截次数呢？

sentences.en: I mean, you said that they do tens of millions of stops a year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你刚才说过他们每年进行数千万次拦截。

sentences.en: Well, a part of the answer is money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分答案是金钱。

sentences.en: Two of my other colleagues in investigations, Mike McIntyre and Michael Keller, were really intrigued about the incident where police in Virginia had pulled over
sentences.zh: 我的另外两位调查记者同事迈克·麦金太尔和迈克尔·凯勒，对弗吉尼亚州警察拦下陆军中尉卡隆·纳扎里奥的事件深感好奇。

sentences.en: Army Lieutenant Caron Nazario.
sentences.zh: 陆军中尉卡隆·纳扎里奥。

sentences.en: They'd pulled him over and pepper sprayed him and threatened him.
sentences.zh: 他们拦下了他，向他喷胡椒喷雾并威胁他。

sentences.en: And my colleagues found that that same week, the town council was questioning the police chief about why ticket revenue was declining.
sentences.zh: 我的同事发现，就在同一周，市议会正在质问警察局长为什么罚单收入在下降。

sentences.en: And they began to wonder, how important was ticket revenue for this town and other towns like it?
sentences.zh: 他们开始琢磨，罚单收入对这个小镇以及其他类似的小镇究竟有多重要？

sentences.en: And what they found was really surprising.
sentences.zh: 而他们发现的结果着实令人震惊。

sentences.en: More than 730 municipalities rely on fines and fees for at least 10% of their revenue.
sentences.zh: 有730多个市镇依靠罚款和收费来获取至少10%的收入。

sentences.en: In one town in Louisiana, that was more than 85% of its revenue.
sentences.zh: 在路易斯安那州的一个小镇，这一比例超过了其收入的85%。

sentences.en: They found a bunch of small towns out there that issue more tickets each year than they have residents.
sentences.zh: 他们发现许多小镇每年开出的罚单数量比当地居民还要多。

sentences.en: That's crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in many of these places, the money they bring in for tickets is going to their own training, to the police benevolent fund, or to other benefits.
sentences.zh: 在其中的许多地方，他们通过罚单筹集的资金都用于他们自己的培训、警察慈善基金或其他福利。

sentences.en: And what's more, they found that the federal government has a role in this.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们还发现联邦政府在其中也扮演了一定的角色。

sentences.en: The federal government gives out $600 million a year to municipalities for traffic enforcement.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府每年向各市镇发放6亿美元用于交通执法。

sentences.en: And to get that money, states have to present plans for their traffic enforcement.
sentences.zh: 为了获得这笔资金，各州必须提交其交通执法的计划。

sentences.en: And in at least 20 of those states, they explicitly evaluate police on the number of traffic stops they make.
sentences.zh: 在其中至少20个州，他们会明确根据交通拦截的数量来对警察进行考核。

sentences.en: In some towns, cops are told outright, you have to make this many stops per hour.
sentences.zh: 在一些城镇，警察甚至被明确告知：你每小时必须完成这么多起拦截。

sentences.en: So they're directly financially incentivized to be making a lot of traffic stops.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在财务上受到直接刺激，要去进行大量的交通拦截。

sentences.en: Yeah, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And some of these towns that rely disproportionately on ticket revenue were also disproportionately stopping black drivers.
sentences.zh: 其中一些过分依赖罚单收入的城镇，也 disproportionately（不成比例地）拦截黑人司机。

sentences.en: For example, in the town of Newburgh Heights, that's about a half square mile town with 2,000 residents just south of Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 例如，在纽堡海茨镇，那是一个位于克利夫兰以南、面积约半平方英里、拥有2000名居民的小镇。

sentences.en: Tickets account for more than half of their town revenue.
sentences.zh: 罚单占了他们镇收入的一半以上。

sentences.en: 22% of the town's residents are black.
sentences.zh: 该镇22%的居民是黑人。

sentences.en: And yet, black people make up 76% of their license and insurance violations and 63% of speeding cases driving through the town.
sentences.zh: 然而，在驾照和保险违章中，黑人占了76%，在驶过该镇的超速案件中占了63%。

sentences.en: So basically, this is a primarily white town right outside of Cleveland.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这是一个位于克利夫兰郊外的主要是白人的城镇。

sentences.en: They send a lot of troopers out to the highway, and they catch a disproportionate number of black drivers on their way down the highway getting out of town.
sentences.zh: 他们派出了大量州警去到高速公路上，在黑人司机驱车离开克利夫兰驶离小镇的路上，抓获了不成比例的大量黑人司机。

sentences.en: When my colleagues asked about the disproportionate number of black drivers they were pulling over on the road out of Cleveland, the mayor said,
sentences.zh: 当我的同事问及他们在驶出克利夫兰的路上拦下不成比例的黑人司机一事时，市长说：

sentences.en: we don't really control who drives through our community.
sentences.zh: 我们其实无法控制谁开车穿过我们的社区。

sentences.en: We also talked to a former police officer and criminologist who's African-American, and he said he thought that traffic stops were a kind of special problem for racial bias.
sentences.zh: 我们也采访了一位身为非裔的前警察兼犯罪学家，他说他认为交通拦截是种族偏见的一个特殊问题。

sentences.en: As he put it, police think traffic stops are dangerous, police think black people are dangerous, and the combination is volatile.
sentences.zh: 用他的话说，警察认为交通拦截很危险，警察认为黑人很危险，两者的结合是极具爆炸性的。

sentences.en: And add to that what you just said, which is that officers are incentivized to run up the numbers, stop a lot of cars to get money from fines.
sentences.zh: 再加上你刚才所说的，即警察受到激励去刷高数据、拦截大量车辆以获取罚款资金。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, advocates for the police would say, look, traffic stops are important because it gets dangerous drivers off the road.
sentences.zh: 现在，警察的拥护者会说，看呐，交通拦截很重要，因为它能将危险驾驶员清除出道路。

sentences.en: And the risks to police are real.
sentences.zh: 而且警察面临的风险是真实存在的。

sentences.en: So courts and the public need to make special allowances for the fact that those police have to make tough, split-second, life-or-death decisions under pressure.
sentences.zh: 因此，法院和公众需要给予特殊宽容，因为这些警察必须在压力下做出艰难的、瞬间的、生死攸关的决定。

sentences.en: And other people, including judges and juries, shouldn't be second-guessing those choices.
sentences.zh: 而其他人，包括法官和陪审团，不应该事后诸葛亮地去质疑这些选择。

sentences.en: Critics of the police would say if there were more accountability, if more agencies and officers were punished in some way or held liable for the avoidable killing of drivers,
sentences.zh: 警察的批评者会说，如果有更多的问责制，如果有更多的机构和警察因可避免地杀死司机而受到某种惩罚或承担责任，

sentences.en: then they would have an incentive to cut it out.
sentences.zh: 那么他们就会有动力改掉这个毛病。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what we found.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你我们发现了什么。

sentences.en: When we looked through these cases, we found that of the 400 unarmed drivers killed by police at vehicle stops that we had identified,
sentences.zh: 当我们翻阅这些案件时，我们发现，在我们已确认的因交通拦截被警察杀害的400名无武装司机中，

sentences.en: in those cases, only about 30 officers were charged with a crime.
sentences.zh: 在这些案件中，只有大约30名警察被指控犯罪。

sentences.en: And in those roughly 30 cases, only five police officers have been convicted of any crime.
sentences.zh: 而在大约30起案件中，只有5名警察被判定犯有任何罪行。

sentences.en: One of them was given probation and no jail time.
sentences.zh: 其中一人被判缓刑，无需坐牢。

sentences.en: And another one of those five was Derek Chauvin for the killing of George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 这五人中的另一个人是德里克·沙文，因杀害乔治·弗洛伊德而获罪。

sentences.en: In the vast majority of the cases that we looked at, the officers who had killed these unarmed drivers suffered no penalty or consequences.
sentences.zh: 在我们调查的绝大多数案件中，杀死这些无武装司机的警察没有受到任何惩罚或后果。

sentences.en: In many cases, the officers were praised for their conduct.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，警察反而因其行为受到了表彰。

sentences.en: One case that stood out for us was the case of Deputy Jason Hanratty.
sentences.zh: 有一个引起我们注意的案件是副警长杰森·汉拉蒂的案件。

sentences.en: In January of 2019, he joined a chase, along with several other deputies, of a GMC Yukon that had initially been pulled over for a broken taillight.
sentences.zh: 2019年1月，他与其他几名副警长一起，加入了一场对一辆GMC育空SUV的追逐，该车最初是因为尾灯损坏而被拦截的。

sentences.en: The GMC Yukon led them on a wild chase across the county.
sentences.zh: 这辆GMC育空带着他们在整个县疯狂追逐。

sentences.en: Finally, one of the deputies forced it to spin out on a lawn.
sentences.zh: 最终，其中一名副警长逼迫它在草坪上打转停下。

sentences.en: And at that point, Deputy Hanratty got out of his own police vehicle to try to approach the SUV.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，副警长汉拉蒂下 了自己的警车，试图靠近这辆SUV。

sentences.en: It lurched forward again, and the video of that encounter shows that he reached out his left arm, he put it on the hood, and pushed off.
sentences.zh: 它再次向前猛冲，该遭遇的视频显示，他伸出左臂，放在引擎盖上，然后推开。

sentences.en: And at that point, he's arguably safe.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，他可以说已经是安全的了。

sentences.en: The GMC is moving by him.
sentences.zh: GMC正从他身边驶过。

sentences.en: But he pulled out his sidearm with his right hand, and he fired several shots into the driver's side window.
sentences.zh: 但他用右手拔出配枪，对着驾驶员侧车窗开了几枪。

sentences.en: Injuring the driver, a 20-year-old pregnant woman, and passing through her to kill her passenger.
sentences.zh: 打伤了驾驶员——一名20岁的怀孕女性，并穿透她的身体杀死了她的乘客。

sentences.en: Now, that's an avoidable death.
sentences.zh: 瞧，这是一起本可避免的死亡。

sentences.en: And yet, a few months later, the sheriff promoted Deputy Hanratty to sergeant.
sentences.zh: 然而，几个月后，治安官却将汉拉蒂副警长晋升为警长。

sentences.en: The next year, the sheriff awarded him a Medal of Valor.
sentences.zh: 第二年，治安官授予他英勇勋章。

sentences.en: And in the ceremony, his actions were praised as truly heroic.
sentences.zh: 在授勋仪式上，他的行为被赞为真正英雄般的壮举。

sentences.en: David, thank you.
sentences.zh: 大卫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Sunday, leaders of the group of 20 nations, including the U.S., the European Union, and China, sent a symbolic message on efforts to control climate change.
sentences.zh: 周日，包括美国、欧盟和中国在内的二十国集团领导人，就控制气候变化的努力发出了象征性的信号。

sentences.en: Meeting in Rome, the leaders pledged to work to restrict the global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius by the end of the century.
sentences.zh: 领导人们在罗马会晤，承诺努力在世纪末将全球气温升幅限制在1.5摄氏度以内。

sentences.en: The number is seen as a critical threshold for limiting the most severe effects of climate change.
sentences.zh: 这一数字被视为限制气候变化最严重影响的关键门槛。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 并且……

sentences.en: The United States and the European Union have reached a major breakthrough that will address the existential threat of climate change,
sentences.zh: 美国和欧盟达成了一项重大突破，将应对气候变化的生存威胁，

sentences.en: while also protecting American jobs and American industry.
sentences.zh: 同时保护美国的工作岗位和美国的工业。

sentences.en: President Biden struck a deal to roll back tariffs on European steel and aluminum imports,
sentences.zh: 拜登总统达成了一项协议，取消了对欧洲钢铝进口的关税，

sentences.en: resolving a bitter trade dispute with the EU, which began under President Trump three years ago.
sentences.zh: 从而解决了与欧盟之间长达三年、始于特朗普总统时期的激烈贸易争端。

sentences.en: In return, the EU will drop its retaliatory tariffs on American goods, like orange juice, bourbon, and motorcycles.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，欧盟将取消对美国商品（如橙汁、波旁威士忌和摩托车）的报复性关税。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Claire Tannesketter, Muj Zady, and Sydney Harper.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由克莱尔·塔内斯凯特、穆杰·扎迪和悉尼·哈珀制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Larissa Anderson and Michael Benoit, and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由拉里萨·安德森和迈克尔·博努瓦剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Rochelle Bonja, Dan Powell, and Alicia Baitoup.
sentences.zh: 包含罗谢尔·邦贾、丹·鲍威尔和艾丽西亚·拜托普的原创音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brumberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由 Wonderly 的吉姆·布鲁姆伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日秀》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尔尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党便陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时又扣人心弦的权力之争。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，由我萨拉·凯尼格为您讲述那些试图维持影响力却在过程中失控的人们的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都市。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
